title: Oxidation states and half-equations; Orbitals and electron configuration
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: RX01#t1 term and clue written for the game; RX01#t4 term and clue written for the game; RX01#t3 term and clue written for the game; RX01#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AS04#N.3a, RX01#N.6a, AS04#N.6a, RX01#N.11a, AS04#N.9a, RX01#N.13, AS04#N.12a, RX01#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Redox
items.clue: A reaction in which loss and gain of electrons happen together.

items.label: Reduction
items.clue: Gain of electrons, as when each O atom goes from 0 to −2 during rusting.

items.label: Reducing agent
items.clue: The reactant that gives electrons away, like Zn in Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu.

items.label: Oxidation number
items.clue: Value that is 0 for an uncombined element and equals the charge for a simple ion such as Fe³⁺.

questions.stem: What is the maximum number of electrons that a 3d sub-shell can hold, and why?

options.text: 20 electrons, as its ten orbitals can each hold two electrons of opposite spin
18 electrons, as the n = 3 shell holds a maximum of 2n² electrons
10 electrons, as its five orbitals can each hold two electrons of opposite spin
2 electrons, as the 3d sub-shell is one orbital that holds a single pair

questions.explanation: Five orbitals × two electrons of opposite spin = 10.

questions.stem: Chlorine reacts with aqueous iron(II) ions: 2Fe²⁺(aq) + Cl₂(aq) → 2Fe³⁺(aq) + 2Cl⁻(aq). Which species is the oxidising agent in this reaction?

options.text: Fe²⁺, since it loses electrons and so is itself oxidised
Cl₂, since it gains electrons and so is itself reduced
Cl⁻, since it is the species holding the gained electrons
None, since no species here gains or loses any oxygen atoms

questions.explanation: Chlorine's oxidation number falls from 0 to −1: each Cl₂ gains two electrons from Fe²⁺. The species that accepts electrons is the oxidising agent.

questions.stem: Which full electron configuration of a ground-state atom is correct?

options.text: scandium: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s² 4p¹
cobalt: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁹
iron: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁶ 4s²
germanium: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹² 4s²

questions.explanation: 18 electrons to 3p⁶, then 4s², then six in 3d: 26 in all.

questions.stem: In acidic solution, MnO₄⁻(aq) is reduced to Mn²⁺(aq) and Fe²⁺(aq) is oxidised to Fe³⁺(aq). In the balanced overall redox equation, what amount of Fe²⁺ reacts with 1 mol of MnO₄⁻?

options.text: 1 mol
5 mol
2 mol
3 mol

questions.explanation: Mn goes from +7 to +2, so each MnO₄⁻ gains 5 electrons; each Fe²⁺ loses 1. The iron half-equation is multiplied by 5.

questions.stem: An iron atom (Z = 26) has the condensed electron configuration [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s². How is an Fe²⁺ ion formed from this atom?

options.text: Two of the six 3d electrons are removed from the atom.
One 4s electron and one 3d electron are each removed.
Two electrons are added to the 3d sub-shell of the atom.
Both of the 4s electrons are removed from the atom.

questions.explanation: Transition metal atoms lose 4s electrons before 3d: [Ar] 3d⁶, 24 electrons.

options.text: Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂
2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO
2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂
NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O

questions.explanation: O in H₂O₂ is −1 (a peroxide). It goes to −2 in H₂O (reduced) and to 0 in O₂ (oxidised): one element in one species, both ways.

questions.stem: A ground-state phosphorus atom is [Ne] 3s² 3p³. Where are its three 3p electrons?

options.text: Together in one 3p orbital, which all three share.
On one circular orbit at a fixed distance from the nucleus.
Two paired in one 3p orbital, one in a second, the third left empty.
One in each of the three 3p orbitals, with parallel spins.

questions.explanation: Three equal-energy orbitals, three electrons: one each, spins parallel. Each electron is spread over its dumbbell-shaped region.

questions.stem: In the thermite reaction, aluminium reacts with iron(III) oxide: Fe₂O₃(s) + 2Al(s) → Al₂O₃(s) + 2Fe(l). What happens to the iron?

options.text: It loses electrons: iron is always oxidised when it reacts, as it does in rusting.
It gains electrons: its oxidation number falls from +3 to 0, and aluminium supplies them.
It loses electrons to aluminium, since aluminium gains the oxygen during the reaction.
It gains electrons: its oxidation number falls from +6 to 0, as Fe₂O₃ has two Fe atoms.
